_comment: THIRD-PARTY VENDORED SOURCE. This directory is not ours. It is the published
ScaleformUI_Assets.zip from upstream release 5.8.1, extracted whole, plus the
two local patches listed below -- both in loader.lua -- and nothing else. Every
other byte here except LICENSE and this file came out of that zip, whose sha256
is recorded below, so the next upstream bump is: download the new
ScaleformUI_Assets.zip, extract it over this directory, then re-apply those two
tools/verify.sh reads this file. The `vendored third-party` gate checks that
the LICENSE is present, that every BR-PATCH marker in the tree is declared
here and every patch declared here is present in the tree, and that
tools/deploy.sh actually syncs this resource to the box -- because shipping
a resource that never reaches the server is a failure mode this project has
already had twice. `patches` below must keep naming every BR-PATCH marker in
this directory, and nothing else here may be edited without an entry joining
THIS IS THE HALF THAT MAKES THE OTHER HALF WORK. ScaleformUI_Lua requests
compiled Flash movies by name at start; this resource is what streams them.
license_note: Same notice as the sibling ScaleformUI_Lua: Creative Commons
share alike, and NO COMMERCIAL USE. The owner decided on 2026-09-08 that our
LICENSE here is an ADDED file. Upstream keeps its notice at the repository
root as LICENSE.txt and this zip does not contain it, so the notice was copied
in verbatim and renamed to the name CC expects and verify.sh looks for. It and
VENDOR.json are the only two files here that did not come out of the zip.
why_this_resource_exists: Upstream's README states it in as many words: 'This also requires an Assets
resource from the Github Repo Releases, it will not work without them.' The
library is pure Lua that drives compiled Flash movies; the movies are these
files and they ship only as a release artifact, never in the git tree.
stream/ is a FiveM convention rather than a manifest entry -- everything in it
is registered as a streamed game asset automatically, which is why
fxmanifest.lua declares only files/MINIMAP_LOADER.gfx (loaded by handle, not
streamed) and loader.lua. Do not 'fix' the manifest by adding the stream files
THIS IS THE FIRST STREAMED ASSET IN THE PROJECT. README.md's line about the
gamemode using stock GTA V assets with no streamed files was amended on
2026-09-08 to say so rather than deleted.

contents.stream/ScaleformUI.gfx: the main menu movie -- UIMenu and everything built on it
contents.files/MINIMAP_LOADER.gfx: minimap overlay movie, added via AddMinimapOverlay by loader.lua rather than streamed
contents.loader.lua: 12 lines: owns the single minimap overlay handle and hands it out on the ScUI:AddMinimapOverlay event

provenance_check.claim: Every file here except LICENSE, VENDOR.json and loader.lua is byte-identical to the corresponding member of the release asset ScaleformUI_Assets.zip, sha256 recorded below. loader.lua differs by the two BR-PATCH blocks listed under `patches` and by nothing else -- a removed print, an added parameter name, and their comments.
how: sha256sum ScaleformUI_Assets.zip   # must equal release_assets below
diff -r /tmp/sfa/ScaleformUI_Assets 'resources/[scaleformui]/ScaleformUI_Assets' -x LICENSE -x VENDOR.json   # loader.lua is expected to differ, by BR-PATCH 1 and BR-PATCH 2 and nothing else
provenance_check.note: The .gfx files are compiled Flash movies -- magic bytes 'GFX\b' -- and are pinned `binary` in .gitattributes. That pin is not decoration. This repository sets `* text=auto eol=lf`, and while git's own heuristic would almost certainly classify a .gfx as binary, 'almost certainly' is not a property to hang a streamed asset on: one CRLF substitution inside one of these files is silent corruption that every gate here would pass and only a playtest would find. The same argument is already written out for *.ogg, which arrived with pma-voice.

patches.what: Removed a bare, unconditional print(overlayID) from the event handler. Nothing replaced it -- the handle is already returned to the caller through cb.
patches.why: It printed a raw number with no label into every client's F8 console at start, with no way to turn it off. That is the same player-facing fault, in the same shape, that pma-voice's BR-PATCH 1 removed; unlike pma-voice this resource has no logger to route it through, and the value is of no interest to anybody who is not debugging this file, so the line is simply gone.
patches.upstream_fixable: yes -- leftover debug output, would be accepted upstream as a bug fix

patches.what: Added the missing `cb` parameter: exports('AddMinimapOverlay', function() ... end) is now function(cb). One word. The body is unchanged.
patches.why: The export body is a copy of the event handler above it, which takes a callback, but the export was declared with no parameters at all -- so its cb(overlayID) call reached for a global named cb that has never existed, and calling this export died with 'attempt to call a nil value'. NOTHING WE SHIP CALLS IT -- ScaleformUI_Lua uses the event, not the export -- so this repairs a fault we do not currently hit. It was fixed rather than recorded-and-left because the fix is one word and restores the contract the body was already written for. Note what it does not do: a caller must still pass a callback, because that is what the body expects; the export does not return the handle.
patches.upstream_fixable: yes -- would be accepted upstream as a bug fix. Upstream might instead prefer `return overlayID`, which is the idiomatic shape for an export; that would change the calling convention rather than restore it, so it is upstream's call to make and not ours.

untouched_on_purpose: loader.lua -- everything outside the two BR-PATCH blocks. Both faults reported at vendoring time were fixed on the owner's instruction the same day; see `patches`. What is deliberately NOT touched is the design around them: one overlay handle for the whole client, created on first request and handed to every caller afterwards, and the guard being `overlayID == -1` rather than a check on the native's return. That is upstream's, it works, and changing it would be a rewrite of the only file here that is not a compiled movie.

fxmanifest.lua -- as shipped. It declares only files/MINIMAP_LOADER.gfx and loader.lua; the stream/ directory is registered by FiveM convention, not by the manifest, so adding those files to it is not a fix.
